title: Receptionist
description:
Receptionist

Location: Cambridge, CB5 8 PA
Salary: Competitive, DOE
Contract: Full-time, Permanent- Monday to Friday (with participation in the weekend rota required)

About Peasgood & Skeates

Peasgood & Skeates is a long-established, family-owned independent funeral directors with a proud history of serving families and communities across Essex, Cambridgeshire, Suffolk and the surrounding areas.

We understand that losing someone you care about is one of the most difficult experiences in life. Our role is to provide families with care, compassion and professionalism at every stage, and our people are at the heart of delivering that service.

We are now looking for an experienced Receptionist to join our flagship Cambridge office.

About the Role

As our Receptionist, you will be the first person a bereaved family meets and will play a vital role in creating a warm, welcoming and supportive experience.

This is much more than a traditional reception role. You'll combine front-of-house responsibilities with a varied administrative workload, coordinating appointments, handling enquiries, supporting Funeral Directors and liaising with a range of external contacts.

You'll need genuine warmth and emotional intelligence, alongside the ability to remain calm, organised and professional when dealing with sensitive situations and competing priorities.

What You'll Be Doing
- Welcoming bereaved families, visitors and members of the public with warmth, dignity and discretion.
- Handling telephone enquiries sensitively, including initial calls following a death.
- Managing appointments, viewings and chapel of rest arrangements.
- Coordinating diaries and information between families, Funeral Directors and third parties.
- Liaising with clergy, celebrants, crematoria, cemeteries, doctors, coroners, florists and other suppliers.
- Preparing, completing and maintaining funeral paperwork and records accurately.
- Handling payments, invoices and account queries.
- Managing incoming and outgoing post, email and general correspondence.
- Ensuring reception, meeting rooms and public areas are maintained to an excellent standard.
- Providing wider administrative and branch support as required.
- Handling highly sensitive information with absolute confidentiality and in line with GDPR and company procedures.
- Supporting local community activities, events and fundraising where required.

What We're Looking For

Essential:
- Proven experience in a front-of-house or receptionist role this is mandatory.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- A warm, professional and empathetic telephone manner.
- High emotional intelligence and the ability to respond appropriately to people who may be distressed or grieving.
- Strong organisational and administrative skills with excellent attention to detail.
- The ability to remain calm and composed while managing multiple priorities.
- Competent IT skills, including Microsoft Office, with the confidence to learn new systems.
- Absolute discretion, integrity and professionalism.
- A smart and professional appearance and manner.
- A flexible, helpful approach and genuine commitment to providing excellent service.

Desirable:
- Previous or current experience within the funeral industry.
- Knowledge of Cambridge and the surrounding area.
- Experience dealing with funeral-related organisations or third parties.
- Experience in another client-facing role involving sensitive or emotionally challenging situations.
- Full UK driving licence.

A Role That Makes a Difference

This is a rewarding opportunity to become an important part of a team supporting families during some of the most difficult moments of their lives. The role can be emotionally demanding, and you may occasionally come into contact with the deceased, so we ask applicants to consider this carefully.

In return, you'll join a well-established family business with a strong reputation for care, professionalism and service, where the contribution you make to families and the local community genuinely matters.

If you're an experienced receptionist who combines professionalism with compassion, discretion and genuine warmth, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today with your CV and a short covering note explaining why this opportunity appeals to you.

No agencies please.

description: We are looking for an organised, proactive and approachable Undergraduate Medical Education Administrator to join our Medical Services team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong administrative skills who enjoys working with a range of people and supporting high-quality education and training within an NHS environment. This role would suit someone who is confident in managing competing priorities, has excellent communication and organisational skills, and is able to provide a professional and responsive service to students, educators and internal colleagues. To provide dedicated administrative support for undergraduate medical education within CPFT, with a primary focus on coordinating psychiatry placements, teaching programmes, and student experience.The post holder will act as the main point of contact for undergraduate medical students and the Clinical School, supporting the planning, delivery and evaluation of placements and teaching sessions, and ensuring students are able to meet their curriculum requirements. The role will involve close liaison with consultants, clinical teams and teaching faculty to coordinate placements, manage timetables, support teaching delivery, and oversee key administrative processes such as student assessments, onboarding and finance claims.During periods where undergraduate activity is reduced, the post holder will contribute flexibly to the wider work of the Medical Education Team, including support for postgraduate education, induction programmes and general administrative functions. Please refer to the attached job description and person specification for full details of responsibilities. Serve as a primary point of contact within the Medical Education Department, acting as a key liaison between CPFT, the Clinical School, consultants and undergraduate students. Provide comprehensive administrative support across undergraduate (primary focus) and postgraduate medical education activities, including responding to queries,arranging meetings, booking rooms and coordinating teaching sessions. Support the Medical Education Coordinator with Resident Doctor induction and wider Medical Education activities as required. Coordinate undergraduate psychiatry placements, including developing and disseminating timetables and placement allocations, liaising with consultants to establish availability, and organising suitable clinical learning opportunities. Coordinate clinic schedules and allocate students to appropriate clinical sessions, including CAMHS and Drug & Alcohol services. Act as the main administrative contact for undergraduate students during placements, supporting their experience and monitoring completion of requirements, including chasing signoffs and case documentation. Provide administrative support for undergraduate teaching programmes, including lived experience and communication skills sessions, liaising with tutors, actors and individuals with lived experience, and managing session allocation and room bookings. Support student onboarding processes, including facilitating access to CPFT IT systems, SystmOne (S1) and Smartcard IDs in collaboration with the Clinical School and relevant teams. Process student and lived experience tutor expense claims (e.g. travel) and maintain accurate financial records. Collate student assessment outcomes and upload results to university systems in line with required processes and deadlines.

title: Administrator
description: We are looking for a motivated, organised, and personable administratorto join our busy GP surgery. This is a varied and rewarding role that plays a vital part in supporting both our clinical team and our patients. The successful candidate will be responsible for a range of administrative duties, ensuring that patient information is handled accurately, confidentially, and efficiently while delivering a high standard of customer service. Key Responsibilities Processing and managing medical referrals accurately and efficiently. Handling Subject Access Requests (SARs) in accordance with GDPR and practice policies. Preparing and processing medical reports and other clinical documentation. Communicating with patients by telephone, email, and in person in a professional, compassionate, and courteous manner. Liaising with GPs, clinicians, hospitals, and external healthcare organisations. Maintaining accurate patient records using clinical systems. Supporting the wider administration team with day-to-day practice duties. Ensuring all work is completed within required timescales while maintaining confidentiality.
